grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: Passive voice: Simple past
grammarPoints.rule: Use was or were + the past participle when you want to talk about what happened to something, and who did it is unknown or not important.

chart.title: Passive voice: Simple past

intro_examples.text: The Sphinx was built around 2500 BCE.
intro_examples.jp: スフィンクスは紀元前2500年ごろに建てられました。
それは1925年まで発掘されませんでした。
その像はいつ発見されましたか。

rows.example: The Sphinx was built around 2500 BCE.
rows.jp: スフィンクスは紀元前2500年ごろに建てられました。
その像は1974年に見つかりました。
その宝物は盗まれませんでした。
その像はいつ発見されましたか。

rows.example: The treasure was discovered in a field.
rows.jp: その宝物は野原で発見されました。

chart.note_rule: The passive puts the important thing first. The Sphinx matters here, not the builders.
chart.note_exception: Use was with I/he/she/it and a singular noun; use were with you/we/they and a plural noun.
chart.note_exception_detail: Many past participles are irregular: build → built, find → found, steal → stolen, break → broken, take → taken.

table.title: was / were + past participle
notes: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive one.
Make questions by putting was or were before the subject.

grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: Passive voice: Simple past with by + agent
grammarPoints.rule: Add by + the person or thing that did the action when it matters who did it.
grammarPoints.pattern: subject + was / were + past participle + by + agent

chart.title: Passive voice: Simple past with by + agent

intro_examples.jp: その陶器は泥棒に壊されたのですか。

chart.note_rule: The agent is the person or thing doing the action. It comes after by, at the end of the sentence.
chart.note_exception: Only add by + agent when the reader needs to know who did it.
chart.note_exception_detail: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence, and the active subject moves after by.

notes: The active object always becomes the passive subject.
Use by only for the doer — use in, at or on for places.
